clue.text: Complete food, say, from one whose stock is pure

parts.note: complete in the sense of utter or out-and-out, as in a thorough rogue

indicators.note: say signals that the word for food is only heard, its spelling being swapped for a twin of the same sound

parts.note: bread is the staple food, here only spoken

explanation.surface: A recommendation of whole food from someone of pure stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes BREAD a sound-alike: BRED is spelt differently but pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree animal, especially a racehorse, comes from unmixed breeding lines.

clue.text: Historian's account occurring in a holy book

definitions.note: read as 'historian is', the apostrophe-s being a link

indicators.note: occurring in tells us one piece turns up inside another

parts.note: Titus is a book (epistle) of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A historian's record found in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Historian's' looks possessive, but the apostrophe-s stands for 'is' and joins definition to wordplay; 'occurring in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman writer of the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Almost too naive to be moved by applause

indicators.note: letters that are moved get shifted about into a new order
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the phrase goes

explanation.surface: Someone too innocent to be stirred by the crowd's clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last E of naive, leaving TOO NAIV, which 'to be moved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of enthusiastic clapping from an audience.

clue.text: Society member? Not even an associate

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a fellow is a companion or associate

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person belongs to a club and is told they are not even an associate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society, a mutual aid club whose members carry this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Independent Order of Oddfellows, a benevolent fraternity, are known by this title.

clue.text: Blood-covered sword-tip in the furze

indicators.note: covered says one piece wraps round another, here blood around a tip

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: the tip of the sword is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bloodied sword point lies among the prickly shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze and whin are other names for the yellow-flowered spiny shrub of heathland.

clue.text: William F Cody's place in New York State?

definitions.text: William F Cody's place in New York State?

parts.words: William F Cody's place in New York State?
parts.note: Cody was known as ... Bill, and the city on Lake Erie in New York State shares the first part of that nickname

explanation.surface: Where did the Wild West showman live in New York?
explanation.walkthrough: William F Cody, the American showman, was nicknamed after the bison he hunted; that same word is the name of a large city in western New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in New York State bears the same word that formed Cody's famous nickname.

clue.text: Twist together with a fellow in various directions

indicators.note: in says the fellow sits inside the run of compass points

parts.note: E, N and E are three compass points: east, north, east
a twin is one of a matching pair, a fellow

explanation.surface: Winding something about with a companion, going every which way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various directions' looks like an anagram signal, but it supplies three compass points; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to interlace or braid strands round each other.

clue.text: Wycherley's wife's noble lines on a female

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
RY is short for railway, a set of lines
a woman is a female

explanation.surface: A Restoration playwright's heroine is a noble's verse addressed to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: William Wycherley wrote the comedy 'The Country Wife', so his wife is a country woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Wycherley's play is a rural spouse brought to London.

clue.text: Small band find a way to a fruitful area

parts.note: ORCH is a shortened orchestra, a band cut small
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A little group of musicians finds the path to fertile land.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, so literally a fruit-bearing patch.

clue.text: Disproof makes us sort of tearful

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so the word is sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Being proved wrong leaves us somewhat weepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the letters of tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: A refutal is the act of rebutting an argument, showing it false.

clue.text: Age-old yearning to remain inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for remaining within the word for yearning

parts.note: longing is yearning
to stand, as in 'let it stand', is to remain

explanation.surface: An ancient desire to stay indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of many years' standing is long-established, of great age.

clue.text: Sounds like a nocturnal entitlement to salt

indicators.note: Sounds like says the phrase is spoken and the answer spelt as it is heard

parts.note: a night right, a right that holds at night

explanation.surface: A claim to salt that seems to belong to the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a salt of nitrous acid, used for curing meat.

clue.text: Prevarication of state in rejection of report

indicators.note: in places the state inside the turned word
rejection, a throwing back, has the word for report read from the end

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, like a gunshot
VA is Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: Dodging the truth about the nation by dismissing a dispatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' gives ESION, the word for report read backwards; 'in' signals the insertion. Report as a bang, not a document, is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is ducking a straight answer, just as prevarication is.

clue.text: Check sulphur content in this compound

indicators.note: content means contained, so the sulphur is held inside

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A chemist tests how much sulphur this substance holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky organic substance from plants, a mixture of chemicals.

clue.text: Bin-ends from port deliveries

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
overs are sets of six deliveries (balls bowled) in cricket

explanation.surface: Wine sold off cheaply from shipments of port.
explanation.walkthrough: Bin-ends are the last few bottles of a wine sold off cheap; in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bin-ends are the remaining odd bottles of a stock, surplus to the rest.

clue.text: Having. to follow a river straight away

indicators.note: to follow says the having word comes after the river

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river
with means having, as in 'a man with a hat'

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to trail a river at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth is a river in Scotland, flowing into the Firth of Forth at Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith means immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Desire king to hold wartime prisoner and show some determination

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the prisoner sits within

parts.note: will is desire or wish
ER, Edwardus Rex, is a king's royal cipher
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A ruler wants to keep a captive and display resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: WILL and ER together hold POW: WILL-POW-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is resolve or strength of mind.

clue.text: A flat-bottomed barge is more buoyant

definitions.meaning: a vessel used to carry cargo between ship and shore

explanation.surface: A cargo boat floats higher than others.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a harbour boat for unloading ships and the comparative of 'light' meaning weighing less.

clue.text: Super, to change shape as he could!

definitions.text: Super, to change shape as he could!

indicators.note: the two words alter their form, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A marvel, the mythic figure could alter his form at will.
explanation.walkthrough: Proteus, the Greek sea god, could change shape at will; 'change shape' rearranges SUPER and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea god of Greek myth shifted form to escape anyone who tried to question him.

clue.text: Mate is member of the watch in admiral's ship

annotationWithheld.why: Mate is member of the watch in admiral's ship (5) for CHINA: 'Mate' gives CHINA as rhyming slang, but no reading of 'member of the watch in admiral's ship' could be found that builds the letters or a second definition
annotationWithheld.clue: Mate is member of the watch in admiral's ship

clue.text: Reservoir where bird is caught? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: this tells us to reverse the order of the pieces the clue lays out, so that the catch comes first

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A water tank where a bird gets trapped, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where bird is caught' gives TERN IS C; 'Quite the opposite' flips the order to C IS TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water.

clue.text: The type inclined to be emphatic

definitions.text: The type inclined to be emphatic

parts.words: The type inclined to be emphatic
parts.note: reads like a description of a forceful personality, but type is printing type, sloping and used for emphasis

explanation.surface: A person who tends to stress every point.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping printed letters are used to put stress on a word.

clue.text: Plant commonly found near the Scrubs

definitions.text: Plant commonly found near the Scrubs

parts.words: Plant commonly found near the Scrubs
parts.note: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison; the plant meant is a close relation of wormwood, with the botanical name vulgaris, meaning common

explanation.surface: A weed that grows freely near the London prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison. The plant meant, Artemisia vulgaris, is a close relative of wormwood; 'commonly' points to vulgaris, Latin for common.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugwort is the common artemisia, a weedy aromatic herb.

clue.text: Into a ship comes the old poet

parts.note: T' is the clipped northern dialect form of the, as in 'on t' moor'
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: An ancient poet comes aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance poet of 'Jerusalem Delivered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian epic versifier.

clue.text: Spouse has American bishop under control

indicators.note: under control means held within it, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: to have a hand in something is to control it
US is the United States, American
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A partner keeps a US clergyman in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under control' reads as a phrase about discipline, but 'under' signals the pieces going inside the word for control.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a married man, one half of a couple.

clue.text: Jack abandons toads — engages in idle gossip

indicators.note: abandons means leaves behind, so the named word drops out

parts.note: natterjacks are a European species of toad
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks away from some amphibians, then chatters.
explanation.walkthrough: The natterjack is a European toad; take JACK out to leave the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly, to chinwag.

clue.text: Spanish secret police chief entering sophisticated milieu

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the chief sits inside

parts.note: the in crowd is a fashionable, sophisticated set
Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's NKVD secret police

explanation.surface: A Spanish spymaster joins a smart set.
explanation.walkthrough: Beria ran Stalin's secret police; IN means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian describes the peninsula of Spain and Portugal, so broadly Spanish.

clue.text: Greek writer's circle in Athens. and Paris, oddly enough

definitions.note: read as 'Greek writer has', the apostrophe-s being a link

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters fall in an odd new order

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A Greek dramatist's set in Athens and in Paris, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' rearranges O with ATHENS and PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the comic playwright of ancient Athens, author of The Frogs.
